result.summary: In 2018 LeCun's dated predictions on record come from his printed interview in Martin Ford's Architects of Intelligence. He said a self-supervised breakthrough in learning how the world works could take two years or 10 to 20, probably about 10, and that AGI 'might take 50 years, it might take 100 years'. He also said cheap deep-learning hardware would put AI in everyone's hands within 2 or 3 years. The 2018 news coverage I opened (CNN, a Forbes headcount story) held no further dated AI predictions.

reply_text:
Decode the PDF and extract text.I found four dated predictions from 2018. All come from one source: LeCun's printed interview in Martin Ford's book *Architects of Intelligence* (Packt Publishing, copyright 2018). I read them in a full copy of the book hosted on a UCLA faculty page. That copy is not the publisher's own edition, so you may want to check the quotes against the printed book. The book does not give the day of the interview. Ford asks a question that says "Now, in 2018", so I've dated everything "2018".

**The four predictions**
- **Machines learning how the world works from video:** a breakthrough "in two years", or "10 or 20 years". He adds that he has "no idea when it will happen."
- **That breakthrough and its real-world effect:** "probably" 10 years, and he says it "has to happen way before" human-level AGI.
- **AGI:** "might take 50 years, it might take 100 years, I'm not too sure."
- **AI in everyone's hands:** "in the next 2 or 3 years", because of hardware built for deep learning. This one is borderline. It rests on chips, but what it predicts is that AI will be widely available, so I kept it and flagged it.

**Left out on purpose**
- **Self-driving cars "in the next five years":** he describes this as what investors are hoping for, not his own forecast.
- **The job market shifting "over the next several decades":** this is about the economy, not about AI doing something.
- **Facebook's AI lab doubling in size by 2020** (Forbes, October 2018): a company headcount plan. I saw this only in a search snippet and didn't open the page.
- **The book's survey of when AGI arrives:** the answers are anonymous, so none of them can be tied to LeCun.

**Pages that didn't help**
- **Forbes, July 2018 profile:** it opened, but only the site's menus came back, not the article. Nothing is quoted from it.
- **CNN, December 2018:** it opened, but it's a news write-up with no dated prediction in it.
- **NYU page "decades away" from human-level intelligence:** it turned out to repeat a Wall Street Journal piece from April 2017, so it's listed under other_years.

**Accounting**
- **Searches:** all 12 used. The three fixed searches ran exactly as written, once each. The first one's results came back in an unexpected format and broke my display code, so I read the stored results instead of running it again.
- **Page openings:** 4 of 6 used.
